generalizable_features.reason: Diurnal consumer meal and shopping rhythms follow universal cyclical daily curves across Indian cities.
Weekend leisure footfall spikes are structurally consistent across all metropolitan markets.
Thermal comfort response (suppressed outdoor footfall at > 40°C) is universally observed.
Precipitation universally suppresses mobile street-vendor demand across all geographies.
Relative ratio of commercial to residential zoning generalizes regardless of city scale.
Fundamental category economics (food vs salon vs repair) exhibit consistent demand elasticities.

non_generalizable_features.recommendation: Exclude raw spatial coordinates (lat, lng, h3_cell_id) from multi-city cross-evaluation. For scale-sensitive POI features, use city-specific calibration factors or localized models.

generalization_limitations: Scale Disparity: Tier-1 IT metropolitan centers (Bengaluru, Hyderabad) operate at 25%-35% higher baseline footfall volumes than Tier-2 cities (Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam).
Microclimate Variations: Visakhapatnam experiences marine humidity and coastal sea breezes; Bengaluru features an elevated 900m plateau climate with evening rain showers.
Cultural Diurnal Shifting: Hyderabad dining and street-food peak between 21:00-00:00 (late evening culture), whereas Vijayawada peaks earlier between 19:00-21:30.
Commuting Patterns: Bengaluru vendor demand clusters heavily along Metro and Tech Park feeder roads (Outer Ring Road, Electronic City), requiring transit-aware spatial weighting.
Simulated Data Notice: Current cross-city benchmarks utilize simulated scale adaptation; real-world city deployments require a 14-day local data collection calibration window.
conclusion: Multi-city generalization benchmark confirms: Zero-shot transfer from Vijayawada to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, and Visakhapatnam incurs a mean MAE penalty of +16.4%. Applying city-specific calibration factors ({'vijayawada': 1.0, 'hyderabad': 1.2478, 'bengaluru': 1.3498, 'visakhapatnam': 1.0512}) recovers 53.05% of the transfer penalty. A pooled multi-city model achieves near-localized precision (MAE 1.6128 vs 1.2470) while maintaining a single operational deployment.
